_README: LAUNCH CONFIG for sparrowmap.com on a public box. Copy over config.json
there - do NOT use it on the LAN hub, it will lock you out of the review
page until you sign in with the token from data/operator.token.
Every value below differs from the development config for a reason that is
written next to it. The defaults in core.py are tuned for a hub on a
private tailnet where the only person who can reach it is the owner; a
public box inverts almost every one of those assumptions.
_operator_requires_auth: THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST. Off, the operator check trusts the socket
address - and behind nginx or Caddy EVERY request arrives from 127.0.0.1,
so every visitor on the internet becomes an operator: able to retract
sightings, promote a private vehicle onto the public map, and confirm one,
which is what makes a plate searchable. Launching without this publishes
a stranger's ability to publish strangers.
_behind_tls: Adds Secure to the operator cookie. Only set it when TLS actually
terminates in front of the hub, or the cookie is set and never returned,
which reads as 'login is broken' rather than 'you need https'.
_public_mirror: THE ARCHITECTURAL CONTROL, and the reason a breach of this box is not a
catastrophe. On a mirror: node TRUE positions are never stored, private
vehicles keep no image, no plate hash and no description - only an
anonymous dot for the live traffic view - no training crops are written,
and the operator routes do not exist at all. What an attacker copies is
the published government record, which is already published.
Reviewing, labelling and retraction happen on the home hub.
_auto_approve_nodes: ON, matching the live box (Matthew's decision 2026-10-28: intended). A new
camera posts the moment it enrols, so a volunteer is on the map without
waiting for the operator. The cost: anyone who finds /api/enroll can add a
camera, so a bad one is dealt with after the fact (revoke_node.py, owner
/api/node/remove). This file is the deploy default (DEPLOY.md copies it to
config.json), so a rebuilt box keeps the behaviour it has today. Set false
to make new cameras arrive 'paused' (tools/approve_node.py lets one in).
_publish_public_tier: Start OFF on the public box. Turn it on once the head has run there for a
few days and the review queue is clean. An empty map is recoverable; a
wrong one is what this project exists to not be.
_map_center: Where the public map opens. Deliberately a rounded, region-level point:
a shipped config must never carry the coordinates of a real camera, and a
street-level default centred on one is exactly how that leaks. Set it to
the area you cover, not to a camera.
_retention: civilian_retention_days is the promise on the About page. public 0 means
government sightings are kept - they are the record the project exists to
produce. Run /api/purge on a timer; it is operator-only now.
